column1: # The two distinguishable values axis C writes, one per side of a dispute.
# WHY THIS FILE AND NOT `forms.tsv`. That table fixes a SINGLE magnitude, 7331,
# because axis A asks about the FORM of a value and one value per form is
# enough. Axis C asks who wrote the value that survived, which needs two
# values that can be told apart — and `forms.tsv` is frozen, so the pair is
# declared here instead of by widening it.
# Distinguishability is never assumed. Every row of axis C compares the two
# sides as the product rendered them, and a pair the run cannot tell apart is
# read NOT OBSERVABLE rather than repaired by picking a different number: the
# stand reports what the declaration bought, it does not shop until it wins.
# The magnitudes are far above every threshold default in this tree (the same
# property the 7331 comment states), so a write is distinguishable from the
# key being omitted. `graduated-sibling` is the SECOND slot of a graduated
# pair: a triple needs one slot only the lowest layer writes, and one the
# highest layer writes back, or nothing is at stake in it. Both sibling values
# stay above their primary so that `warning <= error` holds and the write is
# not refused for a reason that has nothing to do with composition.
# `framework-pattern` and `framework-witness` belong to the SECOND observation
# point. `suppress_paths` never reaches the options object — the factory
# drains it into the registry's providers before `fromArray()` — so the value
# is observed by asking the predicate the product's own consumers ask, about
# the witness file each pattern is chosen to match and the other one it is
# chosen to miss.
